newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Dealers say Skellerup rumours ill-informed - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Dealers say Skellerup rumours ill-informed - NZPA.

text.p: Institutional bond dealers said on Monday they remained comfortable with their holdings of Skellerup Finance debt, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
Dealers added that rumours of difficult trading for its Levene subsidiary were neither new nor unexpected.
"We're relatively comfortable," one dealer, who declined to be identified, said.
"Levenes and Palmers (Gardenworld) are actually very small parts of the overall business. The problem is they are probably the most publicly visible part of the business.
"We believe that Masport and some of the more substantial parts of the business are doing all right," he said.
Yields on Skellerup Finance bonds climbed from 14 percent to 18 percent on Friday on what appeared to be individual retail trades.
On Monday, two trades worth only NZ$22,000 pushed the yields to 20 percent.
Friday's price fall, said to be caused by rumours about the group's performance, prompted a query from the Stock Exchange, on whose fixed interest board the bonds are traded.
The company, whose other subsidiaries include rubberwear maker Skellerup Industries, hire business Projex and miner DML Resources, said it had no explanation for the price fall.
